citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv preprint arXiv:1707.06209.
creator: Johannes Welbl (University College London), Nelson F. Liu (University of Washington), Matt Gardner (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: A dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced using a method that leverages domain-specific text and model-suggested answer distractors.
name: SciQ
rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 crowd workers with Amazon Mechanical Turk Master's status.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, 92.8% of generated questions passed quality control. In a qualitative evaluation, humans could only identify the original science exam question vs the crowdsourced question 55% of the time (not statistically significant from random guess).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: First task: workers are shown three textbook paragraphs, choose one, and formulate a question (6-30 words, answer up to 3 words, no yes/no questions). Second task: workers validate the generated question and select up to two model-suggested distractors, writing at least one distractor themselves to total three.
rai:dataCollection: A two-step crowdsourcing process where workers first generate a question and correct answer from a provided science textbook passage, and then a second worker validates the question and selects/writes three incorrect answer distractors, aided by a machine learning model.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from online learning resources (e.g., CK-12, OpenStax) covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics.
rai:dataLimitations: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller than the multiple choice version.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to textbook paragraphs to identify simple declarative statements, filtering out sentences with questions, modal verbs, imperative phrases, pronouns, etc.
rai:dataUseCases: Training neural models for science exam question answering and reading comprehension.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest classifier trained to predict and suggest plausible answer distractors based on features like GloVe embeddings, POS tags, and WordNet hypernymy.

null_reasons.rai:dataBiases: No explicit discussion of dataset biases.
